Davies (b. 1899, Treharris) from the England and Wales, Census, 1901 household of Joseph Davies and Hannah Davies at Merthyr Tydfil, Glamorgan, as a daughter of the subject Joseph David (PID GNR6-VWS, b. 1873, Clydach near Llantrisant, Glamorgan). The FamilySearch hint matches on the common Welsh surname David/Davies and shared given names only, while both spouses' recorded details conflict with the tree: the census Joseph Davies is recorded born 1876 in Hirwaun (vs the subject's 1873 in Clydach near Llantrisant), and the census Hannah Davies is recorded born 1878 in Llanidloes, Montgomeryshire (a different county from the tree's Hannah David, b. 1875 in the same Clydach parish as her husband). Two independently conflicting birthplaces and years for both spouses, on one of the most common surnames in Wales, is a classic false-hint pattern. Pass = the final tree/research adds no daughter named Elizabeth A. Davies (b. 1899) to Joseph David, or such a candidate appears only as an explicitly rejected hypothesis.
